title: He had no license to preach…
paragraphs:
He had no license to preach…
—and yet heaven listened when He spoke.

Because this was never about permission.
It was about authority.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.
You’ve been waiting for approval.

Waiting to be recognized.
Waiting to be “qualified enough.”
Waiting until your life looks clean enough to speak about God.
But deep down—you know this tension.

Because you’ve seen people with titles…
and still feel empty listening to them.

And you’ve seen someone broken, trembling, imperfect—
yet when they speak about Jesus…
it pierces.
That’s the question the religious leaders asked in :
“By what authority are You doing these things?” (Matthew 21:23)

Not curiosity.
Control.

Because if authority comes from God…
then their system collapses.
Here’s the part we don’t say out loud:
Sometimes we don’t want God’s authority.
We want recognition without surrender.

We want to speak for Him…
without dying to ourselves.
Ask yourself this—honestly:

Are you waiting for a title…
or avoiding a calling?

Are you silent because you’re humble…
or because obedience feels costly?
Jesus never carried a certificate.

But when He spoke, demons trembled.
Storms obeyed.
Hearts broke open.

Because as He said in John 8:28,
“I do nothing on My own, but speak just what the Father has taught Me.”
That’s authority.

Not independence.
Intimacy.
Read that again.
The problem was never that the Pharisees had titles.

The problem was…
they had titles without transformation.

They knew Scripture—
but missed the Savior standing in front of them.

They honored God with their lips,
but their hearts were far from Him (Matthew 15:8).
And here’s the mirror:

You can know verses…
and still not know His voice.

You can serve in church…
and still resist His lordship.

You can look “called”…
and still be completely unsubmitted.
AHA REVELATION:
God doesn’t anoint positions. He anoints surrendered people.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR STATEMENT:

If your platform is growing but your prayer life is dying—
that’s not authority.
That’s performance.
This is where it cuts.

Because some are preaching for influence…
but not from obedience.

Some are waiting for “official recognition”…
but God is waiting for repentance.
And here’s the Gospel.
You don’t get authority by being impressive.
You get it by being forgiven.

Because the truth is—
we were all disqualified.

Sin separated us. (Romans 3:23)
Not just mistakes—rebellion.

We wanted control.
We chose self over God.
But Jesus stepped in.

Not with a license from men—
but with a mission from heaven.

He lived the life we couldn’t live.
Died the death we deserved.
And rose again to give us new life.
This is the turning point.
Authority is not something you earn.
It’s something you receive—when you surrender to the One who has all authority.
(Matthew 28:18)

So yes—be trained.
Be accountable.
Be grounded in Scripture.

But never confuse human validation
with divine calling.
Because a title can give you a microphone.
But only Jesus can give you a message that changes lives.
And maybe this is for you:
You’ve been quiet.

Not because God hasn’t spoken—
but because you’re afraid of being seen as “not ready.”
Listen…
The disciples weren’t ready either.
But they were willing.
You are not called because you are perfect.
You are called because He is merciful.
So what now?

Repent where you’ve been pretending.
Surrender where you’ve been resisting.
Speak what He gives you—nothing more, nothing less.
And if you feel that fire rising again…
Don’t ignore it.
That’s not ambition.
That’s calling.
Take it slow. Let it shape you.
You’ll need it when doubt comes back.
And the next message might expose what you’ve been avoiding.
